title: On the Panagia of the Holy Mountain

pairs.en: *“The Panagia of the Holy Mountain has left her home, has come out of her garden, and has arrived here.”*

sections.heading: The Ark goes forth, and the people follow

pairs.en: We now see that the Panagia of the Holy Mountain has left her home, has come out of her garden, and has arrived here. The Holy Mountain sent her out into the world with great love and tenderness. She offered her Panagia for the veneration and blessing of the people, whom God loves. She offered her treasure — her very treasure.

When the Israelites were about to leave one place and go elsewhere, they would see the shining cloud — the sign of God's presence — lift up and rise. And then the whole people would gather around, in front, behind, to the right and to the left of the Ark. And while everyone shouted for joy, while the trumpets and cymbals sounded, you could see hearts stirred — moved to see the Ark going forward, and the people following behind it. They knew that God was there, and they went where God was.
That is exactly what has happened now with us.

sections.heading: A city comes out to receive her

pairs.en: Just look! Around the Panagia, around this icon which truly represents the presence of the Panagia — what holy excitement! As soon as it appeared on the open sea, it was greeted by the ships, and then the cannon salutes began. First they paid their honors, and then the whole crowd bowed their heads. Men's eyes filled with tears, their knees trembled. Everyone was all eyes, straining to see the Panagia.

And the road filled up, and the pavements, and the balconies — nothing was left empty. The sky held back the rain that day the Panagia came, so that we would have no hindrance at all. Everyone went out to receive the Panagia, the Mother of Life — the one who gives us the courage to go on.

See now how blessed Thessaloniki is — that beautiful and richly graced apostolic see and city — whose God-loving children, from one night to the next, keep coming to venerate the All-Holy Theotokos, the Queen of all the world.

sections.heading: Axion Estin: her rest at the heart of the Mountain

pairs.en: Wonder-working, this Panagia of “Axion Estin” — you already know this very well. She is enthroned in the heart, and at the center, within the sanctuary of the first and of the central church of the whole Holy Mountain.

The monks live by her presence. This work has been going on now for a thousand whole years. She is the chief visible token of the presence of the All-Holy Theotokos within the life and the whole way of being of the Holy Mountain. Almost every monastery of the Holy Mountain has beside it a wonder-working icon of the Panagia. Just as the sun spreads its light and warmth abroad through its rays, so too the all-holy, blessed Mother of God transmits her grace through her many icons.

But all the countless multitude of the Holy Mountain's fathers, who have lived there from the beginning until today, experience the Theotokos whom you see here as a personal event of their own — and there has hardly been one of them who did not have a personal encounter with the Panagia. The monks of the Mountain live together with her; and together with them, the Panagia lives with them too.

The great number of her wonder-working icons shows the Panagia's care for the Mountain — but also the monks' love for the Panagia. Daily supplications to the Theotokos, the Salutations never cease. Litanies one after another, all-night vigils continually. The whole Holy Mountain speaks of the Panagia — of whom it has been said: “She never ceases to be the invincible ally, the provider, the guardian, the physician, the ark, the salvation” — of the monks, and of visitors too.

And she herself, on her own initiative, chose the Holy Mountain to become her allotted portion, her chosen inheritance — and from then on, the Holy Mountain and the Panagia can no longer be separated. They are so joined together that you would think they were one.

sections.heading: Where the mother is, that is home

pairs.en: Some monk of the Holy Mountain, in these very days, went out into the world to see doctors, so as to recover the health he had lost. He got well, and was about to go back in. He didn't know the news from the Holy Mountain — there isn't a monk on the Mountain who doesn't know exactly what is happening now with the Panagia, because she is each one's own mother. He didn't know, and he was sick. And just as he was about to go in, he heard that the Panagia was here, and he said: “But where would I go, when my mother is right here?” And he stayed, so that the Panagia could come in, and he could go in together with her.

sections.heading: The Holy of Holies, and the Mountain's avaton

pairs.en: How the Theotokos, from her childhood, remained within the Holy of Holies — because the Holy of Holies is a type of the hesychast life, of God's drawing near to man. In just this way she continues even now to be the Holy of Holies, and she brings God into our own souls. She is the mother of virginity, and remained the Virgin-Mother. She never sought to occupy herself with anything else but Christ alone, so that she could occupy herself with our own troubled hearts, with our problems, and with the requests of our faith.
The world of the Holy Mountain, then, became the Panagia's portion, because it sought God — and so she decided never to lift up her head, but to bow down before the people.

So she remains on the Holy Mountain, in a place so set apart, so chosen, so entirely beautiful, between earth and heaven, on its borders. She remains, then, on the borders of land and sea, on the frontier of East and West. In this way the Panagia draws close to everything. She has taken her place at the center of human life.

So great, then, is the bond between the Panagia and the Holy Mountain that the two are almost one and the same. She is “higher than the heavens,” and at the same time “the foundation of the earth” — higher than the heavens, and the foundation of our life. She is the true, living Holy Mountain, just as the Holy Mountain is her earthly dwelling — the mountain the prophets speak of, the mountain “not cut by human hand,” the “fat and fertile mountain.” That is what the prophets, in Holy Scripture, ascribe to the Panagia.

That is why it is only natural for the Panagia to find her rest within the Mountain; that is why she is the one and only woman who enters it — and the *avaton* thereby shows itself to be the unbroken mystery of a virgin conception: that is, the mystery of the Panagia's protection, which helps our own life to bear fruit.

She is the only woman who enters the Holy Mountain — and in this way she herself supplies the theological reason for the Mountain's *avaton*. She wants to be alone before her Son and God. Having borne the God-man Christ within her womb, she enclosed and contained within herself the whole of the Godhead, and also the whole of created human nature. That is, the Theotokos, holding within her the whole of God, and holding the whole of human nature — since Christ had taken it up — within herself, within her own womb.
The Panagia can grant us to God, and unite us with Him, and grant God to us. See what the Panagia means; see what a single icon can do.

sections.heading: Her shelter reaches the whole world

pairs.en: So, my beloved, this shows that the shelter and protection of the Theotokos belongs, yes, to the Holy Mountain, but it is not confined there. Rather, the shelter and protection of the Theotokos extends to the whole of humanity, to the whole world. The icon of the Panagia, as we said, is the presence of the Theotokos — but it is, at the same time, also the presence of the God-man, the Craftsman of the world, Christ Himself. It is the presence of God, and it is also our own presence before the icon and before Christ.

The Panagia is within the sanctuary, but her eyes range over the whole world. There she becomes especially perceptible, personally tangible, we might say — but in the same way she is perceptible everywhere. She extends everywhere, and wherever she extends, her Son is granted there too. People who offer their special prayers reach her throughout the whole world — just think how the Panagia's protection embraces all flesh.

But tell me — do you feel the great significance for our life of the mystery of this icon? The Panagia from the Holy Mountain acts upon us too — on you, and on the next person, and on every human being. Just as God in the Divine Eucharist is present in one place, undivided, because He is one God, and yet is broken and shared out among all people — so too the Panagia. Our Panagia is one present Theotokos, one icon, yet she is offered and shared out into the life of all Orthodox Christians. All of us become partakers of her grace; all of us receive what belongs to God; all of us have the gifts of the Panagia's Son.

sections.heading: What the monks have seen with their own eyes

pairs.en: Do you know, my beloved, that on the Mountain they do not only see her protection — but how many times in history has the Panagia herself appeared, not as an icon, but as a whole living person before the monks' very eyes? Full of life, full of tenderness, full of compassion poured out on the people.

And what has the Panagia not done? To some she shows the way; with others she walks alongside; in others she intervenes as their lady. To some monks she gives their wages; and others she rebukes, when they are not good servants. They see her praying; they see her weeping; they even see her serving food, when there is need.

But what is the Panagia? And what does the Panagia not do? She becomes our servant, and serves even our most, we might say, ordinary and human needs. And if she does this for the monks — who, after all, are free of worldly care, who have no problems, no anxiety, no difficulties in their spiritual and communal life — how much more can the Panagia help, and always does help, the person out in the world, who lives with abandonment, who lives with pain, who lives with sickness, with the pressing needs of every day. She is our Panagia of the Holy Mountain, but she is also your own Panagia, brother.

sections.heading: Her silent walk through the streets

pairs.en: Above all, of course, she conveys sanctification and peace, transforms the world — of times and of places — sanctifies homes, blesses our crops, our lands, the air, the earth, everything. Why exactly do we hold processions with holy water? To sanctify the whole place. The procession you saw these past days — what is it? It is the walk of the Lady, the walk through her own estate, the walk of the Queen through her kingdom. She walks. The Queen walks through the streets — that is why we brought her out. And she watches, she listens, she sanctifies, she communes with us, she inspires us, and even more, she communes at every moment with her Son and God.

She moves forward through the procession, and I cannot fully grasp how much her silence itself is saying. She says to her Son: “Here — I want you to pay attention to this; don't forget that one; look at what this person is going through, my Son and my God — please make this happen.” The Mother communes with her Child, who is also our Father and our God.

However silent and quiet and dignified she is, however adorned and glorified she is, just as great and as majestic is her protection over us. She is majestic in her silence. Have you heard her say anything out loud? And yet this silence stirs up our faith and our prayers. She is humble within her glory — within her glory as the one who has triumphed over corruption and death. She is the palace of the unapproachable light.

sections.heading: The whole Mountain comes with her

pairs.en: She passed through the streets of Thessaloniki. She passed, too, through our hearts. Through her, God Himself passed by. He is present. He is present together with the icon, and at the same time the whole Holy Mountain is present too — because the Panagia means the Holy Mountain. The whole Mountain, with all its holiness, its power, and the Church's tradition, has come in here, into the world.

So our Panagia activates the unceasing, night-and-day prayer of the Holy Mountain. It works the mystery — it works the mystery of redemption. It reveals the incarnation of the Word within us, and makes us share in the mysteries of heaven and earth. We who are sinners, we who are weak, passion-ridden, we who are troubled by demons — we enjoy these gifts through the prayer of the Holy Mountain. It activates the human person and draws the whole of creation up into the worship of God. That is why the Panagia came out and visited us in this way.

sections.heading: Her going up, and her promise

pairs.en: *The recording breaks off here, and picks up again only near its close:*

And they will take her with them, together with the countless invisible hosts of the angels. They will take her, and when they arrive there, they will say: “Arise into your rest, O Ark of your covenant.”
But this departure too, my beloved, of our Panagia, is itself a prophecy.
